title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on quality evaluation and regression checks for Lucent Health pilot. Reviewed prompt sets, scoring spreadsheet, recent model regressions after quantization, and guardrail tuning. Agreed on next steps: run expanded eval with adjusted temperature and prompt variants, share updated scoring sheet, provide SOC2/KMS docs and schedule benchmarking run for latency/cost with Dedicated config.
action_items: Jordan Price: Send updated scoring spreadsheet and README (due 2026-06-25)
Maya Chen: Run 2k-example eval with temperature 0.0/0.2 and top_p variants + collect hallucination rates (due 2026-06-28)
Aisha Khan: Provide 3 additional production prompts and edge-case examples (due 2026-06-26)
Jordan Price: Share SOC2 summary + KMS integration notes and contact for security review (due 2026-06-25)
Liam O'Connor: Provision test VPC endpoint access for Redwood Private trial (due 2026-07-01)
next_steps: Run expanded regression eval across prompt variants and quantization profiles
Redwood to share scoring sheet and mapping of score -> severity
Schedule 1-hour benchmark for Dedicated config (throughput + p50/p95 latency)
Security team to review SOC2/KMS documents and follow up
Plan canary rollout for guardrail changes post-eval
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Price: Hey everyone, good to see you. thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes. quick intro?
[00:10] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here, head of ML at Lucent. we'll focus on quality evals today.
[00:18] Tom Rivera: Tom, eng manager. short on time but want to hear regression findings.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Maya from Redwood SE — I'll go through the eval results and tunings we ran this week.
[00:30] Jordan Price: Great. Maya, over to you.
[00:34] Maya Chen: OK so the TL;DR: we ran the 1k prompt set you gave plus the 200 curated edge-cases Aisha added. we compared baseline fp16 model on Hosted vs quantized INT4 on Dedicated-like profile. overall quality drop was small but we saw regressions on a handful of templates — notably clinical instructions where the model hallucinated a medication dosage.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: yeah that was our main worry, hallucination in clinical outputs is a no-go. can you show the examples?
[01:11] Maya Chen: sure, I'm pulling the spreadsheet — example id 742, prompt about discharge instructions — baseline score 0.92, INT4 quantized 0.68, human severity marked as high.
[01:26] Tom Rivera: Is that a quantization artifact or prompt mismatch?
[01:29] Maya Chen: likely a mix. quantization exacerbated tokenization edge cases — especially with numeric ranges and units — plus temperature was at 0.7 in that run. we reran with temperature 0.0 and saw hallucination drop but also reduced helpfulness in some open-ended tasks.
[01:48] Jordan Price: So tradeoff — lower temp reduces hallucination but might hurt recall/coverage. any guardrail pattern that helps?
[01:55] Maya Chen: We recommend a multi-pronged approach: (1) lower temperature for clinical templates; (2) canonicalization of units in prompts (we gave examples); (3) add post-hoc rule-based checks — e.g., if output contains a dosage, cross-check with allowed ranges; (4) for high-risk templates, keep on hosted fp16 or dedicated fp16 until we validate INT4 profile.
[02:20] Aisha Khan: That sounds sensible. can Redwood run the eval with temp 0.0 and top_p 0.9 for the clinical set?
[02:26] Maya Chen: Yes — we have that in the action items. we can also run multiple quant profiles and give delta per prompt.
[02:33] Ravi Patel: quick note — Redwood Optimize suggested a different batching config which reduced tokens/sec cost by ~12% but increased average p95 latency by 30ms. worth noting for throughput-focused endpoints.
[02:48] Tom Rivera: latency numbers are important. for synchronous UI calls we need p50 under 200ms ideally. how close are we?
[02:55] Maya Chen: On Hosted API with caching for prefixes you're at ~120–160ms p50 on typical short prompts. Dedicated INT4 config with no prefix cache was around 240ms p50 in our test — but with KV cache enabled it drops to ~170ms. there is tuning required.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: For Private/VPC deployment, we'll need audit logs and KMS integration — can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed keys?
[03:23] Jordan Price: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and we can provide audit log samples. we'll attach SOC2 summary and our KMS notes.
[03:32] Dr. Priya Shah: On PHI — any retention policy changes we should be aware of?
[03:36] Maya Chen: We can configure no-retention for customer data on Dedicated/Private for HIPAA scenarios and we offer contract addenda — we'll surface the legal/security contact.
[03:45] Aisha Khan: Back to scoring — what's the rubric? our team saw the spreadsheet but want mapping of numbers to severity.
[03:52] Maya Chen: The scoring sheet uses 0–1 normalized score: >=0.9 pass, 0.7–0.9 caution, <0.7 fail. we also include columns for hallucination flag, safety flag, and manual notes. Jordan will send the updated sheet.
[04:10] Tom Rivera: Can we automate some guardrail checks at runtime, like metadata tagging and immediate suppression of outputs with certain keywords?
[04:16] Maya Chen: yes that's doable — you can add a post-processing lambda that filters by keywords or do a second-stage classifier call. Redwood supports function-calling style pipelines to integrate that.
[04:29] Aisha Khan: Any blockers on our side to run the bench? we want to test Dedicated with 2 concurrent clients and 500 req/min.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: Need a test VPC endpoint and IAM creds for the perf team. I'll provision and share.
[04:41] Jordan Price: We'll schedule a 1-hour benchmark and provide the test harness.
[04:45] Maya Chen: One more note — we noticed one regression where the model rewrote a patient's allergy list incorrectly after a prompt reframe. that's in the spreadsheet id 801 and flagged as severity medium. likely prompt engineering fix is to force list format and include guardrail to assert list length equals input.
[05:05] Aisha Khan: OK. can you also include a run with the model pinned to an earlier revision? we suspect the change correlates with a recent model version swap.
[05:14] Maya Chen: yes, we ran a quick diff — earlier revision matched baseline more closely for that template. we'll include per-prompt diffs.
[05:22] Jordan Price: Great. recap of next steps: Maya runs expanded eval with temp variants, Jordan shares scoring sheet + SOC2 docs, Liam sets up VPC test access, Aisha supplies more edge prompts. schedule follow-up next week same time. anything else?
[05:38] Tom Rivera: No, thanks all.
[05:40] Jordan Price: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[05:45] (call ends)
